interpretation: Suitability is a bounded engineering compatibility modifier for the v3 formula, not a measured bite probability or proof that surface water equals fish-experienced temperature. Source biology constrains the domain and shape; exact suitability ordinates are conservative calibration judgments.

curves.rationale: Burbot are winter specialists but do not have a single narrow annual optimum: telemetry supports spawning selection below 2 C and nighttime feeding selection around 12-14 C. The plateau therefore remains broad from very cold water through 12 C, then declines quickly above 14 C.
limitations: Spawning aggregation and feeding compatibility are distinct mechanisms represented by one shared curve.
Reservoir telemetry is not a Lake Michigan pier catch-rate study.
Temperatures above 23 C are out of accepted domain and must use the engine's explicit out-of-domain handling rather than extrapolation.

curves.rationale: The Great Lakes Fishery Commission synthesis places growth performance in the upper 20s C, while the USGS spring spawning range near 11-15 C requires a nonzero cool-water shoulder. The curve is intentionally broad because temperature preference varies geographically and spawning is not feeding.
limitations: The 28.5 C growth optimum is not an adult Grand Haven bite optimum.
Local July-October availability is handled by the opportunity mode rather than embedded in this curve.
Out-of-domain temperatures must not be silently clamped into a favorable score.

curves.rationale: White bass use a cool spring migration/spawning window around the mid-teens C but adult preference literature is much warmer. A broad 14-31 C high-compatibility region avoids falsely treating either life-history context as the sole bite optimum.
limitations: Underlying migration, spawning and adult-preference values come from different studies and contexts.
The city-specific June-August schooling window is represented in availability, not temperature suitability.
This provisional curve requires prospective residual review before public promotion.

curves.rationale: Michigan DNR describes bluegill as a warmwater species favoring roughly 18-21 C and spawning around 18 C, while the state literature synthesis reports warmer growth optima. The plateau spans 21-27 C and retains a broad shoulder rather than treating spawning temperature as the only optimum.
limitations: Cover, prey, water clarity and harbor habitat can dominate short-term pier success.
This is an adult/general angling compatibility curve, not a larval tolerance curve.
Local summer availability is separately constrained by Grand Haven evidence.
